videos.script: Every for-each loop in this course has been talking to an object you never saw. This lesson shows it. {{iterator}} It is the iterator. Two methods, hasNext and next, and a position it keeps to itself. The compiler turns every for-each into calls to it, and the bytecode proves it. {{cme}} Then the mistake everybody makes once. Walk a list, remove what matches, and the program stops with an exception whose name mentions concurrency, in a program with one thread. {{quiet}} Worse, move the data around and the same loop finishes without a word, and quietly skips an element. {{safe}} Last, four ways to remove while walking, each one correct, and a table for choosing between them. By the end you can change a collection inside a loop and know the answer is right.
